This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for the State.

This is an application under section 483 of the B.N.S.S., 2023 in connection with Nikirai P.S. Case No.72 of 2019 corresponding to G.R. Case No.932 of 2019 pending in the file of learned Additional Sessions Judge -Cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Kendrapara for alleged commission of offences under section 363/366/376(2)(n)/294/506/64 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 6 of the POCSO Act.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge -Cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Kendrapara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prayer for bail of the petitioners has been rejected by the learned Additional Sessions Judge -Cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Kendrapara vide order dated 26.03.2025.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners were on bail and due to non-taking of steps on the date fixed, non-bailable warrant of arrest was issued against them and thereafter, they were taken into judicial custody and they were granted bail.

But, thereafter there is also default in the appearance of the petitioners for which NBW of arrest was issued against them and since then, the petitioners were taken into judicial custody on 22.03.2025.
He further submits Prafulla Jena vs State Of Odisha ..... Opposite Party

sentences.text:
on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150843189/
1 that the petitioners are ready and willing to cooperate with the learned trial Court for early disposal of the case and therefore, the bail application of the petitioners may be favourably considered.

Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the petitioners are flouting the terms and conditions of the bail order repeatedly and, therefore, they may not be enlarged on bail.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the fact that the petitioners were earlier on bail and taking into account the period of detention of the petitioners in judicial custody, I am of the opinion that it is a fit case for grant of bail to the petitioners.

Let the petitioners be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
each (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper to ensure his presence during trial with further condition that the petitioners shall appear before the trial Court on each date when the case would be posted for trial with further condition that each of the petitioners shall furnish cash security of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand).
Violation of any of the terms and conditions fixed shall entail cancellation of bail.
The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Signed by: BASUDEV NAYAK (S.K. Sahoo)
